les: Wat jou hande van 'n materiaal kan uitvind
kaps_punt: onverwerkte en verwerkte materiale het spesifieke eienskappe. Hierdie eienskappe kan hard of sag, styf of buigbare, sterk of swak, lig of swaar, waterdig of absorberende wees

items.bewering: 'n Eienskap is iets wat 'n materiaal doen of is, en waaraan jy dit uitken. 'n Materiaal het sy eienskappe, of iemand dit nou toets of nie. Droë hout bly hard, al vat niemand daaraan nie.
items.bron: Oxford Learner's Dictionaries, 'property' (a quality or characteristic that something has); Wikipedia, 'Intensive and extensive properties' (properties such as hardness and density belong to the material and are used to identify it). A property exists whether or not anyone tests it. The wood part depends on the wood item below.

items.bewering: Die toetse in die eerste blok: druk met jou duim; buig en kyk of dit sy eie vorm hou; skeur van die rand af en kyk of dit heel bly; tel twee ewe groot stukke op; laat 'n druppel water val en kyk of dit intrek; vergelyk stukke van dieselfde grootte.
items.bron: Tested as a set against the six property blocks below: each test matches the definition its own block gives and gives the result the lesson says, with the two exceptions reported separately (balsa wood under the thumb test, moist clay under the drop test). The same-size rule fits lig/swaar (weight depends on volume) and buig (stiffness of a plate or beam goes with thickness cubed: NTNU TMM4175 course notes). One note on wording only: 'kyk of dit sy eie vorm hou' could mean after letting go, and then a springy plastic ruler would look stiff. The block 'Styf of buigbaar' settles it ('buig nie onder jou hande nie'), so nothing here is false.

items.bewering: Die wol op 'n skaap se lyf is sag onder jou hand. Wol is onverwerkte materiaal, en dit het sy eie eienskappe.
items.bron: Wikipedia, 'Cape Wool' (South African wool is a fine, silky staple; most SA wool is Merino); University of Pretoria repository, 'The fibre fineness of South African Merino wool' (most fibres 12.5 to 22.5 micron, the fine range that feels soft); picuino.com 'Classification of materials' (wool as an animal raw material). Raw fleece also carries grease and dust (tis-gdv.de: only about 50% fibre), but it still gives under the hand.

items.bewering: Mense weef lap van daardie wol, en die lap het ook eienskappe. Mense het die wol verander, en daarom is lap verwerkte materiaal.
items.bron: Maine State Museum, 'How to Make Wool Cloth' and 'Wool Production In Depth' (shorn, washed, carded, spun, then woven on a loom into cloth). Leaving out washing, carding and spinning simplifies the method without making it false.

items.bewering: Hout, wol en klei kom net so uit die natuur.
items.bron: picuino.com 'Classification of materials' and the Xunta de Galicia 'Raw materials, technical materials and their manufactured goods' page: wood, wool and clay are the usual plant, animal and mineral examples of raw materials. Sawn wood is sometimes called lightly processed, but treating wood as raw is the usual school convention and not false.

items.bewering: Mense bak klei in 'n baie warm oond, en dan word dit 'n baksteen. Daardie baksteen is verwerkte materiaal en nie meer natuurlike klei nie.
items.bron: Littlehampton Brick (brick clays fired at 1000 to 1150 °C in kilns); webwoordenboek.nl 'Waarom is baksteen duurzaam?' (bricks fired at about 850 to 1200 °C); Middlesex University ceramics project and pottery sources (fired clay can never become plastic clay again). Leaving out the shaping and drying before firing is a fair simplification.

items.bewering: Glas, papier, leer en lap is materiaal wat mense gemaak het.
items.bron: Xunta de Galicia raw-materials page and picuino.com: paper is made from wood, leather from animal skin, and fabric from fibres. Glass is made by melting sand with other substances. Natural glass such as obsidian exists, but the glass meant here is made by people.

items.bewering: Harde materiaal gee nie mee wanneer jy met jou duim daarop druk nie. ... Sagte materiaal gee mee sodra jy met jou duim daarop druk.
items.bron: A working definition for Grade 4 that matches how a material resists being dented (Wikipedia, 'Janka hardness test': the force needed to push a ball into the surface). It sorts the lesson's own examples correctly.

items.bewering: Druk op 'n droë stuk hout en jy maak geen duik daarin nie.
items.bron: Read literally, 'n droë stuk hout' means any dry wood. Balsa is the softest and lightest wood sold commercially (WoodSolutions, 'Balsa'; woodbin.com), and it is sold in craft shops for model-making. 'You can easily crush it. You can score it with your thumbnail' (University of Houston, Engines of Our Ingenuity, episode 233). Model Airplane News has a repair article for dents balsa picks up just from being handled while a model is built. A child doing this test on balsa can make a dent. Ordinary building timber does pass the test. The same claim about all wood comes back in 'Wat 'n eienskap is' ('Droë hout bly hard') and in 'Lig of swaar' ('Die hout is hard onder jou duim')).
items.regstelling: Narrow the quantifier rather than the subject: say that most dry wood, or ordinary dry wood such as a plank or a block, will not take a dent from your thumb. Check that the sentence in 'Wat 'n eienskap is' and the one in 'Lig of swaar' still agree with the narrowed claim. Do not name balsa unless the lesson needs it.

items.bewering: 'n Klein stukkie droë hout is net so hard as 'n groot plank.
items.bron: Hardness belongs to the material and does not change with size (Wikipedia, 'Intensive and extensive properties' lists hardness as intensive), so the idea behind the sentence is true. As written, though, it compares any small piece of wood with any large plank, and kinds of wood differ hugely in hardness: balsa is the softest commercial wood (WoodSolutions), while lignum vitae and ironwoods are among the hardest (Wikipedia, 'Janka hardness test'; woodweb.com). A learner can take the sentence to mean that all wood is equally hard. The lesson already gets this right for plastic ('Een dik stuk van dieselfde plastiek').
items.regstelling: Compare pieces of the same wood: a small piece cut from a plank is just as hard as the plank itself. That keeps the point, that size does not change hardness, without saying that every wood is equally hard.

items.bewering: 'n Gebakte baksteen gee ook nie onder jou duim mee nie.
items.bron: Ceramics are hard and stiff because of strong ionic and covalent bonds (UNSW Materials, ceramics properties tutorial). Firing turns plastic clay into a hard ceramic body (freeflow.yolasite.com kiln notes; webwoordenboek.nl).

items.bewering: Druk jou duim in 'n bondel wol en die wol gee dadelik mee. Vou 'n katoenlap tot 'n dik bondel op die tafel. Druk met jou duim daarop en die dik lap gee mee.
items.bron: Wool is a crimped, springy fibre that squashes and springs back (Merino fibre sources found while searching; the Cape Wool article). A folded pad of cloth is mostly air between the fibres and squashes under a thumb. A child doing this would see what the lesson says.

items.bewering: Sagte materiaal moet dik genoeg wees voordat jy kan voel hoe dit meegee.
items.bron: How far a layer can be pressed in is limited by how thick it is: a single layer of cloth on a table squashes by a fraction of a millimetre, and a thumb barely feels it. The sentence talks about what you can feel in the test and does not say thin cloth is not soft, so it does not clash with the 'small piece is as hard' sentence. It is true of the test described.

items.bewering: Stywe materiaal hou sy eie vorm en buig nie onder jou hande nie. Hou 'n dik stuk droë hout aan albei kante vas en probeer dit buig. Die hout bly reguit en gee nie mee nie.
items.bron: NTNU TMM4175 course notes: how hard a plate or beam is to bend goes with its thickness cubed, so a thick piece of wood cannot be bent by a child's hands. 'dik' is what makes the sentence true, because thin strips of wood do bend. Wood stiffness: WoodSolutions timber data.

items.bewering: 'n Keramiekbord is ook styf, en hy hou sy eie plat vorm.
items.bron: UNSW Materials ceramics tutorial (high elastic modulus); Penn State MATSE 81 and Wikipedia 'Brittleness' (ceramics break rather than bend). A 'plat bord' is the ordinary Afrikaans name for a dinner plate, so 'plat vorm' is fair.

items.bewering: Buigbare materiaal gaan krom onder jou hande sonder dat dit breek. Buig 'n leerriem in 'n boog en die riem volg sommer jou hande. 'n Dun plastieksak buig net so maklik om jou vinger.
items.bron: Oxford Learner's Dictionaries, 'flexible' (able to bend easily without breaking). A belt bends easily by hand. A thin plastic film is hard to bend only to the third power of its thickness (NTNU TMM4175), which is close to nothing for a bag.

items.bewering: 'n Dik stuk van dieselfde plastiek buig nie so maklik soos die sak nie. Daardie stuk is bloot dikker, en die dikte maak die verskil.
items.bron: NTNU TMM4175 course notes: 'Flexural stiffness of plates and beams is proportional to the cube of the thickness'; double the thickness and it is eight times as hard to bend. The material is the same, and only the thickness changed.

items.bewering: Sterk materiaal bly heel wanneer jy daaraan trek of daaraan skeur. Vat 'n leerriem aan albei punte en trek met al jou krag. Die riem bly heel, en jy kry hom nie stukkend nie.
items.bron: Leather Dictionary, 'Tensile strength - Tear strength': cow leather 8 to 25 N/mm². A belt about 35 mm by 3.5 mm (around 120 mm²) therefore takes roughly 1 000 to 3 000 N to break, many times what a nine-year-old can pull with both hands. Test standard ISO 3376:2020.

items.bewering: Swak materiaal skeur maklik en gaan onder jou hande stukkend. Skeur 'n bladsy papier van die rand af en dit gaan maklik in twee.
items.bron: NIST technical paper T194 and BioResources (Lyne et al. 1973) on paper tearing: a tear starts easily at an edge, because the force is concentrated on a few fibres there. A sheet pulled evenly at both ends resists much more, but the lesson calls 'strong' surviving both pulling and tearing, so classing paper as weak follows from its own definition.

items.bewering: Droë hout is ook sterk, en 'n dik stuk skeur nie onder jou hande nie.
items.bron: WoodSolutions timber data: even balsa, the weakest commercial wood, is about half as strong as Baltic pine, and a thick piece cannot be torn by hand. 'dik' carries the claim.

items.bewering: Styf en sterk is nie dieselfde eienskap nie. 'n Leerriem buig maklik, en tog hou hy al jou krag uit.
items.bron: Stiffness (resistance to bending) and strength (resistance to breaking) are different properties in materials science (UNSW Materials tutorial; Wikipedia 'Brittleness': ceramics are stiff yet break easily under tension). Leather figures as above.

items.bewering: Vat 'n blok hout in een hand en 'n ewe groot baksteen in die ander. Die baksteen trek jou hand ondertoe, en die hout voel lig daarnaas. Hout is dus ligter as gebakte klei van dieselfde grootte.
items.bron: Fired clay brick: 1 600 to 2 050 kg/m³ (oneclicklca manufacturer EPDs; TU Delft repository, about 1 880 kg/m³). Even the densest woods are lighter: lignum vitae about 1 260 kg/m³ (Wikipedia, 'Lignum vitae') and black ironwood about 1 355 kg/m³ (Wood Database, via woodworkersjournal.com). Common woods are 400 to 800 kg/m³. The claim holds for every kind of wood.

items.bewering: Hard beteken nie swaar nie, en daardie blok hout wys dit. Die hout is hard onder jou duim, en tog voel dit lig.
items.bron: Density and hardness are separate properties (Wikipedia, 'Intensive and extensive properties'). Ordinary wood is hard and also less dense than brick (figures above). This rests on the thumb-test claim for wood reported above. It is true for ordinary wood, so it needs to stay consistent with that fix.

items.bewering: 'n Groot plank hout is swaarder as 'n klein stukkie gebakte klei. Daardie plank is bloot groter, en sy gewig vertel jou niks oor die materiaal nie. Vergelyk dus stukke wat ewe groot is wanneer jy hulle optel.
items.bron: Mass equals density times volume (Wikipedia, 'Intensive and extensive properties': mass and volume depend on size). A plank of about 10 litres weighs about 5 kg even at 500 kg/m³, and 1.5 kg even as balsa. A 50 cm³ piece of brick weighs about 0.1 kg. Weight on its own, without size, says nothing about the material.

items.bewering: Waterdigte materiaal laat nie water na die ander kant deur nie. Sit 'n druppel water op die buitekant van 'n plastiekemmer. Die water bly buite en kom nie deur die plastiek nie. Wat binne die emmer is, bly droog.
items.bron: Oxford Learner's Dictionaries, 'waterproof' (does not let water through); plasticsintl.com HDPE data sheet and plasticranger.com (polyethylene water absorption about 0.1%, so in practice it lets no liquid water through). A child doing this sees a dry inside.

items.bewering: 'n Glasbottel hou water op dieselfde manier binne.
items.bron: British Glass knowledge base, 'Glass containers - protective packaging for foods': glass is a complete barrier to liquids, vapours and gases.

items.bewering: Absorberende materiaal trek water by homself in en hou dit vas. Laat 'n druppel op 'n katoenlap val en die lap suig hom in.
items.bron: Oxford Learner's Dictionaries, 'absorbent' (able to take in something easily, especially liquid); Sciencing, 'Why Is Cotton Absorbent?' and the Beltwide Cotton Conference abstracts (cotton cellulose draws in water and holds it). A child sees the drop disappear into ordinary cotton cloth.

items.bewering: 'n Klein lappie suig 'n druppel net so goed in as 'n groot lap.
items.bron: How well a cloth soaks up a drop depends on its fibres and weave, not its size (Beltwide abstracts on fibre and web structure). One drop of about 0.05 ml is far below what even a small cloth can hold, so the result looks the same. Unlike the wood sentence, 'lap' here clearly means the same cotton cloth as in the previous sentence.

items.bewering: Ongebakte klei suig water in en word sag daarvan.
items.bron: True of dry clay: dry unfired clay takes up water and softens or breaks down, and can be worked again (Middlesex University ceramics project; pottery reclaim sources). But the sentence says unfired clay in general, and the clay a Grade 4 class usually handles is moist potter's or modelling clay that is already soft and full of water. Wet clay lets water through so slowly that it is used to seal ponds (conservationhandbooks.com, 'Puddled clay'; pondtrademag.com), so a drop on a moist lump stays on the surface and does not soak in. A child doing this test on clay straight from the packet will not see what the lesson says. 'word sag daarvan' only makes sense if the clay started out dry and hard.
items.regstelling: Say that the clay is dry: dry, unfired clay soaks up the drop and goes soft where it got wet. Only add that moist clay is already soft if that costs nothing.

items.bewering: 'n Gebakte baksteen suig ook water in, en tog bly hy hard.
items.bron: Fired clay bricks absorb roughly 10 to 20% of their dry weight in water (IS 1077 limit 20%; ASTM C67 test method; SNRU and JEAS studies, mean 17.45%). Firing below the sintering temperature leaves brick porous (webwoordenboek.nl; freeflow.yolasite.com: bisque at 950 to 1000 °C 'will absorb water'). Fired clay does not turn plastic again, so it stays hard.

items.bewering: Een materiaal het gewoonlik verskeie van hierdie eienskappe tegelyk.
items.bron: Every material can be described on each of these scales at once, so 'gewoonlik' understates it rather than overstates it. This is shown by the lesson's own examples (brick hard and absorbent, leather flexible and strong, wood hard and light) and by the glass sources below.

items.bewering: Die glas is hard, en dit gee nie onder jou duim mee nie. Die glas is styf, en die glasruit hou sy eie plat vorm. Die glas is waterdig, en die reën loop aan die buitekant af.
items.bron: British Glass knowledge base (glass is a complete barrier to liquids); glasstile.com 'The unique nature of glass' (non-porous, takes in no liquid); Wikipedia 'Brittleness' and UNSW Materials (glass is hard and stiff, and breaks rather than bends). Pressing a thumb on a window pane is safe and shows no give.

items.bewering: Parallel set test: the six property blocks and the glass block, read together for false contrasts.
items.blok: Hard of sag; Styf of buigbaar; Sterk of swak; Lig of swaar; Waterdig of absorberend; Een materiaal met verskeie eienskappe
items.bron: Every material placed on one side of a pair is never placed on the other side anywhere else. Where a material has two properties that might look opposed, the lesson says so itself (brick hard and absorbent, leather flexible and strong, wood hard and light), so no false contrast is implied. The size and thickness sentences agree: hardness and absorbency do not depend on size, while stiffness and weight do depend on thickness and size, which is correct (NTNU h³; intensive versus extensive properties). The only set-level fault is that 'droë hout' is treated everywhere as hard under the thumb, which fails for balsa (item above). No superlatives appear in the lesson ('net so hard', 'net so goed' and 'met al jou krag' are comparisons, not superlatives), and there is no analogy to check for its mapping.

items.bewering: begrip eienskap: Iets wat 'n materiaal doen of is, en waaraan jy dit uitken.
items.bron: Read on its own: Oxford Learner's, 'property' (a quality or characteristic that something has). Properties are what identify a material (Wikipedia, 'Intensive and extensive properties').

items.bewering: begrip styf: Materiaal wat sy vorm hou en nie maklik buig nie.
items.bron: Read on its own: Oxford Learner's, 'stiff' (firm and difficult to bend). The entry is accurate.

items.bewering: begrip buigbaar: Materiaal wat krom gaan onder jou hande sonder om te breek.
items.bron: Read on its own: Oxford Learner's, 'flexible' (able to bend easily without breaking). The entry is accurate.

items.bewering: begrip waterdig: Materiaal wat nie water deurlaat nie en die ander kant droog hou.
items.bron: Read on its own: Oxford Learner's, 'waterproof' (does not let water through). The entry is accurate.

items.bewering: begrip absorberend: Materiaal wat water by homself intrek en dan nat word.
items.bron: Read on its own: Oxford Learner's, 'absorbent' (able to take in something easily, especially liquid). Limiting it to water is a simplification and not false.

items.bewering: begrip onverwerkte materiaal: Materiaal wat mense net so in die natuur kry.
items.bron: Read on its own: picuino.com and the Xunta de Galicia page (raw materials are taken directly from nature, unchanged or only slightly changed). The entry is accurate.

items.bewering: begrip verwerkte materiaal: Materiaal wat mense verander het sodat dit ander eienskappe kry.
items.bron: Read on its own: Xunta de Galicia page (processed or technical materials are raw materials changed by people). Processing changes properties, for example clay into brick: hard, no longer plastic (Middlesex ceramics). The entry is accurate.

opsomming: Three claims are contradicted and each needs one narrowing fix: the thumb test does not leave every dry wood undented (balsa dents easily), a small piece of wood is only as hard as a large plank if it is the same wood, and only dry unfired clay soaks up a drop and goes soft (moist clay from a packet does not). Everything else is confirmed, the property blocks contain no false contrast when read as a set, the lesson has no superlative or analogy, and no item is uncertain.
